summary: Rewrites OidcFederationStrategy from one cached CTS token for the whole strategy to one token per provider JWT (SHA-256 keyed, bounded LRU of 1024, pending tier, cancellation guard, strategy-wide account-refusal memory). The provider callback is now called on every get_token, persisted tokens are stamped with federated_from and served only to the matching JWT, and the JS wrappers call getJwt in the caller's async context and hand it to a new getTokenForJwt. Bindings (napi, wasm, Go) gain an optional cache capacity. The change fixes a cross-user identity-binding defect (#1045) and is extensively unit-tested (tests exist, not run here). Residual release risk: (1) the shipped docs and skills now say one long-lived strategy serves every user, but on the @cipherstash/stack native entry protect-ffi calls getToken from a Neon background task where request AsyncLocalStorage is not visible, so the fix only holds there under a documented workaround (#1065 open); (2) the provider now sits on the hot path of every token fetch (and, in Go, under the strategy mutex), so IdP latency or errors now affect every operation; (3) exchange volume to CTS rises with JWT rotation, and an account-level refusal is now remembered across all JWTs. No observed defect found in the core cache logic.

behaviour_changes.description: OidcFederationStrategy keeps one refresh engine per distinct provider JWT (keyed on SHA-256 of the whole JWT) instead of one shared cached token, so callers presenting different JWTs never receive each other's CTS token.

The OidcProvider / getJwt / Go OIDCProvider callback is now invoked on every get_token (before any cache lookup) rather than only when a CTS token must be minted, and must return the JWT of the user behind the current request.

Federated tokens are stamped with a new serialized field federated_from (hex SHA-256 of the JWT); a TokenStore-loaded token is served only to the JWT whose digest it carries. Tokens stored by earlier releases (no stamp) are a cache miss and re-federated once.

New public API: Rust get_token_for_jwt and builder cache_capacity, Token::federated_from; napi getTokenForJwt and optional cacheCapacity argument on create/createWithStore; wasm-inline cacheCapacity option and getTokenForJwt; Go WithCacheCapacity.

The Node and wasm-inline wrappers' getToken() now call getJwt in the caller's JS async context and pass the JWT to getTokenForJwt, instead of the native side calling getJwt through a napi ThreadsafeFunction (async context of create()).

Account-level refusals (USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ORG_NOT_PROVISIONED) are remembered strategy-wide and returned to any new JWT without an exchange for the denial TTL; credential refusals drop the engine and take no cache slot.

Shipped READMEs and agent skills change guidance from 'one Encryption() client per request/user' to 'one long-lived strategy serves many users; a module-level strategy is fine', with a caveat for the @cipherstash/stack native entry.
stack-auth adds sha2 0.10; lockfiles of detached workspaces updated.

failure_scenarios.title: Shared @cipherstash/stack client following the new 'one strategy serves every user' guidance still binds operations to the wrong user on the native entry
failure_scenarios.trigger: A Node server builds one long-lived Encryption() client with an OidcFederationStrategy (as the updated skills/README now encourage: 'a module-level strategy is fine') and either reads the user from AsyncLocalStorage in getJwt, or follows the doc example's closure `() => getUserJwt(req)` while caching the client beyond that request.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: protect-ffi calls strategy.getToken() from a Neon channel background task (encryption/index.ts comments, head). The wrapper's getToken() runs getJwt in that task's async context, where the request's AsyncLocalStorage is not visible (acknowledged in index.ts:800-805 and SKILL.md caveat, #1065 open). A closure that captured one request's `req` returns that user's JWT for every later caller. The per-JWT cache then faithfully serves the captured user's token to everyone.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Either loud failure (getJwt finds no request) or, in the captured-closure case, ZeroKMS operations for user B authenticated and audit-logged as user A, so lock-context identity binding is wrong: the #1045 defect persists on the most common consumer path for anyone who reads the general guidance but misses the caveat.

failure_scenarios.title: Provider callback on the hot path: IdP latency or errors now hit every operation, serialized under the Go strategy lock
failure_scenarios.trigger: A provider whose Token/getJwt call is slow, makes a network request (e.g. an oauth2 token source near refresh, a workload-identity fetch) or fails transiently, in a service with many concurrent encrypt/decrypt calls.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: get_token now calls provider.fetch() before any cache lookup (oidc_federation_strategy.rs:389-396), whereas the base returned the cached token without calling the provider (base :88-95). In Go, Strategy.Token holds s.mu for the whole guest call (strategy.go:184-193) and the provider runs inside it (transport.go:27-32), so every Token call on a strategy waits on the previous caller's IdP call.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Throughput drop and added p99 latency on every ZeroKMS operation; a transient IdP error fails operations that previously would have been served from a valid cached CTS token. Recoverable, but an availability regression on upgrade.

existing_verification.description: Rust test a_provider_failure_is_returned_before_any_exchange and each_jwt_gets_its_own_token_and_the_provider_is_asked_every_time pin the new contract.

missing_verification: No latency/concurrency test for a slow provider under concurrent Token calls in Go.
No measurement of per-call provider cost with real SDKs (Clerk, oauth2.TokenSource).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Release-note the contract change prominently (the title's '!' is the only breaking marker for Go/Rust callers); recommend a caching provider (oauth2.ReuseTokenSource); consider fetching the JWT outside the Go strategy mutex.

failure_scenarios.title: JWT rotation multiplies CTS exchanges and can trip a strategy-wide usage-limit lockout
failure_scenarios.trigger: An IdP that rotates session JWTs far faster than the ~15 min CTS token lifetime (short-lived session tokens), a provider that mints per call, or a store shared by several users (one slot), at production traffic.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The cache is keyed on the whole JWT, so every rotation is a new engine and a new /api/authorise exchange (changeset lines 35-37); a shared single-slot store now misses whenever the user changes. If CTS answers USAGE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, settle() records it strategy-wide (oidc_federation_strategy.rs:249-272) and engine_for returns it to every new JWT for the denial TTL.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Higher CTS request volume and usage-metered cost after upgrade; at the limit, every user whose JWT rotates in that window is refused until the TTL passes. Cached users continue to be served.
missing_verification: No estimate of exchange volume per user for the supported IdPs' rotation intervals.
No monitoring identified for /api/authorise rate or eviction/denial logs (eviction is only logged at debug).
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Before release, estimate exchange rate with the shortest-lived supported IdP tokens and confirm CTS rate/usage limits; monitor /api/authorise volume after rollout; consider raising eviction logging above debug.

evidence.claim: get_token calls provider.fetch() first, then get_token_for_jwt looks up the per-JWT engine and verifies workspace.
BoundStore serves a stored token only if its federated_from matches the JWT digest; save writes to the single shared slot.
engine_for checks cache, then pending, then a fresh strategy-wide denial; settle caches on success, drops on failure and records account refusals for all JWTs.
Encryption passes config.authStrategy to protect-ffi newClient, which invokes getToken() on every ZeroKMS request.
Doc states one strategy serves every user, but on the native entry getJwt runs from a Neon background task and cannot see AsyncLocalStorage (#1065); example captures req in the closure.
Shipped skill now says a module-level strategy is fine and one long-lived strategy serves many users, with a caveat for @cipherstash/stack native.
Strategy.Token holds s.mu for the full guest call.
OIDCProvider is asked on every Strategy.Token call and runs while the ProfileStore is locked.
At base get_token returned the single AutoRefresh-cached token; the provider was only consulted on refresh.
ownGetJwt defines an own getToken() that awaits getJwt in the caller's context and calls getTokenForJwt.
Changeset: stored JSON carries federated_from, unstamped tokens re-federated once; JWT rotation faster than CTS lifetime re-federates on each rotation; cache 1024 by default.
JwtRefresher::refresh federates the held JWT and stamps federated_from with its digest.
Builder gains public cache_capacity.
Only UsageLimitExceeded and OrgNotProvisioned count as account refusals.
sha2 0.10 added as a dependency.
